title: Pandas and Data Cleaning
summary: Load a messy CSV of students' marks into a pandas DataFrame, diagnose its problems with .info() and .describe(), and clean them with astype, fillna and drop_duplicates.
objectives: Load a CSV file into a DataFrame with pd.read_csv()
Diagnose missing values, a wrong-type column and duplicate rows with .info(), .describe(), .isna() and .duplicated()
Document what was found and what was fixed

segments.title: What you will build
segments.body:
## What you will build

Real data is rarely tidy. In this lab you get `marks.csv`, a fictional file of marks for 8 students in 5 subjects, and it has three problems hidden inside: three marks are blank, one mark was typed as `85 ` with a stray space after it (so pandas treats the whole column as text), and one row was pasted twice. You will load the file with `pd.read_csv()`, use `.info()` and `.describe()` to find the problems, and then fix them one by one: `.astype(float)` to turn the text back into numbers, `.fillna()` to fill the blanks with the column average, and `.drop_duplicates()` to remove the extra row. Finally you will write down what you found and fixed, the way a careful data scientist does. Filling blanks with 0 would drag the average down, so use the mean instead.

lab.title: Clean the messy marks file
lab.objective: Load marks.csv, diagnose a text column, missing marks and a duplicate row, fix all three with pandas and document the fixes.
lab.instructions:
The file marks.csv (columns student, subject, marks) is in your working directory. Write a program that:

1. Loads it with df = pd.read_csv("marks.csv").
2. Diagnoses it. Print these four lines, then call df.info() and print(df.describe()):
Rows before: 41
Marks dtype before: object
Missing marks before: 3
Duplicate rows before: 1
(use len(df), df["marks"].dtype, df["marks"].isna().sum() and df.duplicated().sum()).
3. Cleans a copy called clean (clean = df.copy()), in this order:
   a) clean["marks"] = clean["marks"].astype(float)  - the column becomes numbers again
   b) fill the missing marks with the column mean: clean["marks"].fillna(clean["marks"].mean())
   c) clean = clean.drop_duplicates()
4. Prints the same four lines for clean with the word after (Rows after: 40, Marks dtype after: float64, Missing marks after: 0, Duplicate rows after: 0) and then Average mark: 72.0 (round the mean to 1 decimal).
5. Documents the work: make fixes, a list of three sentences in your own words, one per problem (the missing marks, the text column, the duplicate row), each saying what you found and how you fixed it. Print each one as Fixed: <sentence>.
lab.constraints: Use pandas. Keep the names df, clean and fixes. Fill missing marks with the column mean, not 0, and do not drop those rows. Keep the four lines in the exact format shown. No input().
lab.starter_code:
import pandas as pd

# 1. Load marks.csv into a DataFrame called df


# 2. Diagnose: print the four "before" lines (rows, marks dtype, missing marks, duplicate rows),
#    then call df.info() and print(df.describe())


# 3. Clean a copy: clean = df.copy()
#    a) fix the marks column type with .astype(float)
#    b) fill the missing marks with the column mean using .fillna(...)
#    c) remove the duplicate row with .drop_duplicates()


# 4. Print the four "after" lines and the average mark (rounded to 1 decimal)


# 5. Document: fixes = a list of three sentences (missing marks, text column, duplicate row)
#    and print each one as "Fixed: <sentence>"
hints: After df = pd.read_csv("marks.csv"), df["marks"].dtype tells you the column type, df["marks"].isna().sum() counts blanks and df.duplicated().sum() counts repeated rows. df.info() shows all of this at once.

Clean a copy: clean = df.copy(). Convert first, because you cannot take the mean of text: clean["marks"] = clean["marks"].astype(float). Then clean["marks"] = clean["marks"].fillna(clean["marks"].mean()) and finally clean = clean.drop_duplicates().

Print the after lines the same way as the before lines but using clean, then print("Average mark:", round(clean["marks"].mean(), 1)). Put your three sentences in fixes = ["...", "...", "..."] and loop: for fix in fixes: print("Fixed:", fix).

visible_examples.description: Spotting missing values and duplicates in a tiny table
visible_examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Asha"], "marks": [70.0, None, 70.0]})
print("Missing:", df["marks"].isna().sum())
print("Duplicates:", df.duplicated().sum())
clean = df.drop_duplicates()
print("Rows after:", len(clean))

lab.solution:
import pandas as pd

# 1. Load the messy file
df = pd.read_csv("marks.csv")

# 2. Diagnose before cleaning
print("Rows before:", len(df))
print("Marks dtype before:", df["marks"].dtype)
print("Missing marks before:", df["marks"].isna().sum())
print("Duplicate rows before:", df.duplicated().sum())
df.info()
print(df.describe())

# 3. Clean a copy
clean = df.copy()
clean["marks"] = clean["marks"].astype(float)
clean["marks"] = clean["marks"].fillna(clean["marks"].mean())
clean = clean.drop_duplicates()

# 4. Check after cleaning
print("Rows after:", len(clean))
print("Marks dtype after:", clean["marks"].dtype)
print("Missing marks after:", clean["marks"].isna().sum())
print("Duplicate rows after:", clean.duplicated().sum())
print("Average mark:", round(clean["marks"].mean(), 1))

# 5. Document what was found and fixed
fixes = [
    "Found 3 missing marks and filled them with the average mark of the column.",
    "The marks column was text (object) because one mark had a stray space, so I converted it to numbers with astype(float).",
    "Found 1 duplicated row and removed it with drop_duplicates().",
]
for fix in fixes:
    print("Fixed:", fix)
